chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: 'From the best of what you feed your families,' he said: It is as it happens, that in the house there is one who eats more than a mud, and from them there is one who eats less than a mud. And if you wish, you provide them with a side dish (idam). The lowest side dish is salt, the middle is oil, and the highest is meat.

key_terms.إِدَامًا: side dish / accompaniment to the main meal
key_terms.الْمُدِّ: a traditional unit of volume measurement for food

ai.seo_question: What constitutes the 'middle' provision for feeding one's family according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the Quranic command to feed one's family from the 'middle' of what one provides, interpreting it as a flexible standard based on household capacity and individual consumption rather than a fixed quantity. He further specifies that side dishes (idam) follow a similar hierarchy, with salt representing the minimum, oil the middle, and meat the highest tier, thereby offering practical jurisprudential guidance for kaffarah and daily sustenance.
